Read raw ATAC counts into a ChromatinAssay

Source: R/ReadATACData.R
ReadATACData.Rd

Import one explicitly shared peak universe from a sparse matrix and genomic ranges, a 10x ATAC/ARC H5 file, or Matrix Market/peaks BED/barcodes files. SCOP checks and aligns identifiers; Signac creates the native assay. No cells or peaks are filtered, and no resources are downloaded or installed.

Usage

ReadATACData(
  object,
  ranges = NULL,
  metadata = NULL,
  peaks.file = NULL,
  barcodes.file = NULL,
  cell.names = NULL,
  sample = NULL,
  genome = NULL,
  annotation = NULL,
  fragments = NULL,
  fragment.cells = NULL,
  assay = "peaks",
  project = "ATAC",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

object

A numeric sparse peak-by-cell matrix, a local 10x ATAC/ARC H5 path, or a local Matrix Market path. Separate matrices with different peak universes must be recounted before combining; this function never fills unmeasured peaks with zeros. The supported Signac constructor requires at least two cells and two peaks.

ranges

A GRanges in 1-based closed coordinates, required with a sparse matrix. Named ranges are aligned to the matrix row names; unnamed ranges explicitly use matrix row order. Duplicate genomic intervals are rejected.

metadata

Optional data frame with unique row names matching the input matrix cell IDs exactly. Rows are reordered by ID, never by position. Supplied nCount_<assay>/nFeature_<assay> columns must agree with the raw matrix; conflicting QC metadata is rejected.

peaks.file, barcodes.file

Three-column peaks BED and one-column barcode paths, both required when object is a Matrix Market path. Gzip compression is supported. Without companion files a path is read as H5, importing only the explicitly declared Peaks modality from its standard feature table; H5 requires optional hdf5r. BED and 10x H5 peak IDs use 0-based half-open coordinates, converted to 1-based closed GRanges (start + 1, end unchanged).

cell.names

Optional unique final cell IDs, in input column order. For example, explicitly prefix barcodes from separate captures. Suffixes are never removed or guessed.

sample

Optional single sample ID, or a named character vector keyed by input cell IDs, stored as sample metadata. A sample label does not establish biological replication; retain donor/condition/capture metadata.

genome

Optional genome label such as "hg38", checked against known labels on ranges and annotation. This sets a label, not a reference download. Supply seqlengths in ranges for chromosome-bound checks.

annotation

Optional Signac-compatible gene annotation GRanges.

fragments

Optional local fragment path(s). Files must be bgzip compressed and indexed. Signac validates the paths and barcode membership.

fragment.cells

Explicit fragment barcode mapping: a named character vector for one file, or a list of vectors in fragments order. Vector names are final object cell IDs; values are exact barcodes in that file. Multiple files require disjoint mappings covering every imported cell. With one file and no mapping, input matrix barcodes are used unchanged.

assay

Name of the new chromatin assay.

project

Project name passed to CreateSeuratObject().

verbose

Whether Signac prints progress messages.

Value

A Seurat object containing a Signac ChromatinAssay with raw counts.

Details

Signac uses genomic coordinates as feature names. Original matrix feature IDs are retained in assay feature metadata input_peak_id; input barcodes are retained as cell metadata input_barcode. Import provenance is stored next to the data in Misc(object[[assay]], "scop_atac_input").

Fragment files remain external references. saveRDS() does not copy them. After readRDS(), use CheckATACData() to inspect their availability and export its fragments table as a resource manifest. Missing external files do not invalidate otherwise valid matrix-only analysis. Update moved paths explicitly using Signac's UpdatePath(); paths are never repaired silently.

See also

CheckATACData(), RunStandardWorkflow()

Examples

peaks <- GenomicRanges::makeGRangesFromDataFrame(data.frame(
  seqnames = c("chr1", "chr1", "chr2"),
  start = c(1L, 101L, 201L), end = c(50L, 150L, 250L)
))
counts <- Matrix::sparseMatrix(
  i = c(1, 3, 2, 3), j = c(1, 1, 2, 2), x = c(2, 1, 3, 1),
  dims = c(3, 2), dimnames = list(c("p1", "p2", "p3"), c("AA-1", "BB-1"))
)
atac <- ReadATACData(counts, ranges = peaks, genome = "hg38", sample = "S1")
CheckATACData(atac)$valid
#> [1] TRUE
